correctionsThisCycle.what: THE FIND OF THE CYCLE — a recurring 53-red count was being carried in the record as a standing environmental caveat, when it was fully clearable in two steps and had been for every cycle that reported it.
correctionsThisCycle.detail: Each verification cycle cloned the branch, saw 51 assertion failures plus 2 suites failing to load, correctly reasoned that neither was a product defect, wrote that reasoning down, and moved on. The reasoning was right and the response was wrong: a caveat that reappears every cycle is a task, not a fact. The 51 are the U/V/W/X/Y suites reading real operator records that are deliberately untracked and therefore absent from a clone — correct behaviour, kept unchanged. The 2 load failures were '@netlify/blobs' missing from node_modules; the dependency is properly declared in package.json, so a clone just needed an install. Copying the 9 real records in and installing the one dependency takes the registry from 436/487 to 514/514. Both steps are now in scripts/verify-clone-prep.mjs.

correctionsThisCycle.what: The prep script is guarded so it cannot become a way to launder a red into a green.
correctionsThisCycle.detail: verify-clone-prep refuses to invent a record: an empty source directory copies nothing and exits non-zero rather than creating a placeholder, and a present-but-empty records directory is reported as not-prepared rather than as a clean tree. Its classifyReds() makes the verdict a function of the tree's state and never of the size of the number — one red on a PREPARED tree is real and can never be called environmental, while 51 reds on an unprepared tree certify nothing in either direction and must not be recorded as a pass rate. Ten assertions in tests/verify-clone-prep.test.mjs hold that line, registered in the runner so a later cycle cannot quietly soften it.
